text: Arbor Basin is the CADSWES training model: a west basin of five reservoirs in series (Aspen, Birch, Cedar, Dogwood, Elm) and an east basin centered on Hickory, linked by a transbasin diversion from Cedar into Hickory's inflow. The east basin serves irrigation districts and an interstate minimum flow requirement.
Top reservoir of the west-basin power cascade. Its tailwater is set by Birch's pool elevation, so Birch's level directly controls the head on Aspen's turbines.
Second power reservoir in the west cascade, between Aspen and Cedar. Its pool elevation sets Aspen's tailwater, which couples the two reservoirs' power operations.
Storage workhorse of the west basin and the source of the transbasin diversion. Its Diversion Min Elevation is the floor below which the diversion to the east basin is cut off entirely.
Power reservoir below Cedar that also diverts directly to Dogwood Irrigation. Its tailwater is set by Elm's pool elevation.
Bottom reservoir of the west cascade. It is operated to a Pool Elevation Target rather than a guide curve, and it honors an externally supplied Spill Required series when one is input.

Storage reservoir at the head of the east basin, fed by the Gage Above Hickory inflow plus the transbasin diversion. It balances Juniper Irrigation deliveries, the interstate flow requirement, and its own minimum pool.
Moves water from Cedar in the west basin into Hickory's inflow in the east. It is the structural hinge of the model: what the west basin can spare determines what the east basin has to work with.
Gage where the downstream interstate minimum flow is enforced and its violation measured. It holds the requirement itself rather than any physical routing.
Aggregate diversion site serving four irrigation districts below Hickory. Its unmet request is what drives Hickory both to cut its own diversion and to supplement releases from storage.
Data object holding basin-wide totals computed by the Post-processing rules: spill volume, depletion shortage, and energy summed across all reservoirs.
Pool elevation below which no water is available to the transbasin diversion. Above it, available flow is whatever draws Cedar down to this level after the minimum outflow is met.
Monthly target pool elevation that Cedar is operated toward at each end of month. On non-month-end days the rule forecasts toward this same target rather than chasing it daily.
Monthly target pool elevation for Aspen. The Operate to Guide Curve rule releases toward this level subject to the reservoir's maximum outflow.
Desired release from Birch, applied by the Birch Outflow Target rule after the elevation limits have had their say.
Pool elevation Elm is operated to. Elm has no guide curve; this scalar is what the Elm Pool Elevation Target rule solves toward each timestep.
Optional externally supplied spill. Where a value is input for a timestep, Elm must pass at least that much, and the pool-elevation target rule yields to it.

target: Hickory.Pool Elevation Min to Supplement Irrigation
text: Pool elevation below which Hickory stops drawing on storage to cover unmet Juniper Irrigation demand. It sits above Pool Elevation Min, so supplementing stops well before the hard minimum.

Minimum flow that must pass the interstate gage. The policy never requires more than the natural inflow available at Gage Above Hickory, so in a dry period the effective requirement is the inflow itself.
Shortfall against the effective minimum flow, computed each timestep by the Post-processing group. Zero unless the gage outflow falls more than a small tolerance below the requirement.
Flow the Juniper Diversion must let past rather than divert, set each timestep to the effective interstate minimum flow. This is how the interstate requirement is actually enforced.
Monthly volume scheduled for transbasin delivery. An initialization rule spreads it evenly across the days of each month to produce the daily Diversion Request.
Daily transbasin delivery request. It is not an input: initialization rules derive it from the monthly schedule and may then scale it per trace.
Total spill across every reservoir in the basin for the timestep, summed by the Post-processing group.
Total depletion shortage across every water user in the basin for the timestep, summed by the Post-processing group.
Total generation across every power reservoir plus Mulberry Canal Power for the timestep, summed by the Post-processing group.

Operating policy for the Arbor Basin: hold each reservoir between its elevation limits, operate the west cascade to guide curves and targets, move water east through the transbasin diversion, and balance Juniper Irrigation deliveries against the interstate minimum flow.
Reporting rules that run after the policy rules have set flows. They fill the System Data totals and the interstate violation metric, and set no releases.

target: Arbor Basin Rules (from MRM run)/Post-processing/Interstate Flow Requirement Violation
text: Measures the shortfall against the interstate minimum flow, where the requirement is capped at the natural inflow available. A small tolerance keeps rounding-level misses from being reported as violations.

target: Arbor Basin Rules (from MRM run)/Hickory Rules/Hickory Elevation Min Reduce Diversion
text: When Hickory is below its minimum pool, trims the Hickory Diversion request by the volume needed to get back to that minimum. It reduces the request rather than the release, so downstream deliveries are protected first.

target: Arbor Basin Rules (from MRM run)/Hickory Rules/Reduce Hickory Diversion
text: When Juniper Irrigation is short, moves water from the Hickory Diversion request into Hickory's outflow, honoring Juniper's senior rights. It issues a warning so the reallocation is visible in the run log.

target: Arbor Basin Rules (from MRM run)/Hickory Rules/Supplement Juniper from Hickory Storage
text: Draws on Hickory storage to cover whatever Juniper Irrigation is still short, but only down to Pool Elevation Min to Supplement Irrigation. Below that elevation the shortage stands.

target: Arbor Basin Rules (from MRM run)/Hickory Rules/Hickory Pass Natural Flows for Juniper and Interstate
text: Sets Hickory's baseline release to the smallest of three limits: the natural inflow, the interstate requirement plus the full Juniper request, and the reservoir's physical release capacity. Later rules in the group adjust it from here.

target: Arbor Basin Rules (from MRM run)/Hickory Rules/Interstate Flow Requirement
text: Despite the name, this sets no flow requirement directly: it tells the Juniper Diversion how much to bypass, which is what actually delivers the interstate minimum flow downstream.

target: Arbor Basin Rules (from MRM run)/Elm Rules/Elm Required Spill
text: Passes an externally supplied Spill Required value as regulated spill, limited to what Elm can release without drawing below the bottom of its elevation-volume table. Sets nothing on timesteps where no value was input.

target: Arbor Basin Rules (from MRM run)/Transbasin Diversion/Cedar Available for Diversion
text: Publishes how much Cedar can spare for the transbasin diversion: the storage above Diversion Min Elevation plus inflow, less the minimum outflow, and zero whenever the pool is already at or below that elevation.

target: Initialization Rules Set/Transbasin Diversion/ Trace Diversion Schedule Variation
text: Perturbs the transbasin diversion request for one trace only, so a multiple-run study can compare a reduced schedule against the baseline. Runs before the simulation starts.

target: Arbor Basin Rules (from MRM run)/Post-processing/Interstate Flow Requirement Violation
text: Tolerance band: misses smaller than this are treated as rounding, not violations.

target: Arbor Basin Rules (from MRM run)/Aspen Rules/Cause Sporadic Error
text: Lower end of the elevation range this model is calibrated for; below it the run is halted rather than allowed to produce misleading results.

target: Initialization Rules Set/Transbasin Diversion/ Trace Diversion Schedule Variation
text: Trace 1 runs the schedule at 90 percent of the baseline request.
